_doc: The material chain the craftable vehicles and the ship gate run on. Every id here is either something you pick up off the ground (source set, no inputs) or something a station turns other ids into (station + inputs). Nothing in this file is a dead end: every raw id feeds a refined one, every refined one feeds a craft in data/vehicles.json or data/shipyard.json, and tests/shipyard.test.js walks the graph and fails if that stops being true. Names are invented for this playground; no third-party anything.
_contract: js/refine.js and js/resources.js were being written by other hands at the same time as this file. THESE IDS ARE THE CONTRACT between them and the two craft ladders: a furnace that produces iron ingots should call them `ingot_iron`, and a rare element mined out of the ground goes into the materials bag as `el_<key>` using the key from universe/data/elements.json (`el_aetherite`, `el_cryonite`, …). If the refining module lands a fuller table, merge this one into it rather than keeping two — but keep the ids.
_stationDoc: Which structure does the work. The build module owns actually placing them; a craft that names a station it cannot find simply reports that it needs one, which is friendlier than hiding the recipe.

hand.name: Bare hands
hand.desc: Rope, a torch, a lashed raft. Nothing to build first.

furnace.name: Furnace
furnace.desc: Ore and fuel in, ingots out. The first real structure.

kiln.name: Kiln
kiln.desc: Clay to brick, sand to glass, brick to a heat shield.

sawmill.name: Sawmill
sawmill.desc: Logs into planks at a sane rate.

workbench.name: Workbench
workbench.desc: Small fiddly work: wire, tyres, lamps.

alloy_forge.name: Alloy forge
alloy_forge.desc: Two feedstocks and a lot of heat. Steel starts here.

chemical_bench.name: Chemical bench
chemical_bench.desc: Sap, salt and water into things that burn or seal.

assembler.name: Assembler
assembler.desc: Components into machine parts. The gate to everything tier 3.

refinery.name: Refinery
refinery.desc: Reagents and ore into refined compounds.

fuel_synthesiser.name: Fuel synthesiser
fuel_synthesiser.desc: The last structure before the sky opens.

_materialDoc: `value` is a rough worth-per-unit used to price a craft and to prove the vehicle ladder climbs; it is not a shop price. `tier` is how far down the chain it sits. `source` on a material means you gather it rather than make it.

ore_iron.name: Iron Ore
ore_iron.source: outcrops and deep veins, most biomes

crystal_raw.name: Rough Crystal
crystal_raw.source: crystal ground, caves, some meteor falls

sap.name: Gum Sap
sap.source: tapped from big trees; the jungle is full of it

water.name: Water
water.source: rivers, wells, rain catchers, melted ice

scrap.name: Scrap Iron
scrap.source: recycled gear and cleared camps — the bag in data/crafting.json

fuel_burner.name: Burner Fuel
fuel_burner.desc: What a motorcycle, a car, a truck and a powered launch drink. Cheap, smelly, and nothing like what a ship needs.

plate_steel.name: Hull Plate
plate_steel.desc: Rolled, folded and riveted. The hull is made of nothing else.

ceramic.name: Heat Tile
ceramic.desc: Fired twice. It is the only thing between the drive and the rest of the ship.

composite.name: Sealed Weave
composite.desc: Gum over woven fibre over a steel skeleton. It holds pressure, which is the entire job of a tank.

circuit.name: Logic Board
circuit.desc: Wire, glass and a cut lens. It is how the ship knows which way is up.

nullplate.name: Null Plate
nullplate.desc: A hull plate with a board laminated into it. Only the warp coil wants one.

fuel_drive.name: Drive Fuel
fuel_drive.desc: Split water, a burner to start it and a cell to hold the charge. Every flight drinks some.
